$comment: Module map for agent/src and cli/src (round 3 TRAIN 1 landed: directory now equals module). DUO-3493: this is the single per-path {module, layer} source -- tools/layers.json's old hand-maintained path=>layer map was proven to equal this file's per-module `layer` expanded over `files` (zero mismatches over all 225 agent/src files) and was retired; sandbox/tests/offline/guards/regress_agent_src_requires.php's directional layer lint derives its file=>layer map from here directly. `layer_notes` carries layers.json's old free-text rationale for placements a filename suffix would suggest otherwise (e.g. a *Materializer file classified repository, not engine).
rules: Every file under a root belongs to exactly one module directory.

A module has exactly one layer; that is what lets sandbox/tests/offline/guards/regress_agent_src_requires.php's directional layer lint derive each file's layer straight from here instead of a second, separately hand-maintained tools/layers.json (DUO-3493).

Within a root, a module may reference only modules in a strictly lower layer, plus itself; every same-layer or upward edge that exists today is listed in that module's `exceptions` and is a ratchet (may shrink, never grow).
cli modules may reference agent modules named in `depends_on` (written `agent:<Module>`); the agent root must never reference cli.
`entry_points` are the classes other modules already reference; a new cross-module reference to a non-entry-point class is a design change, not a refactor.

Namespaces do not change in this move: agent/src stays `namespace Duo;`, cli/src stays `namespace Duo\Orchestrator;`. The additive classmap (agent/duo-classmap.php, cli/duo-classmap.php) maps FQCN to path, so directory != namespace is legal. Sub-namespaces migrate later, per module, Kernel first.

A reserved (0-file) module carries no `exceptions`: composition across engine modules happens in the surface module (`cli/src/Command/`, `agent/src/Command/`), which is where every verb boundary class lives. The one designed exception is a surface->surface dispatch edge the ladder cannot avoid (agent Command -> Assess); when a reserved module lands, any exception it actually needs is a reviewed map change, not a pre-authorised budget.

layer_notes.src/Apply/TypedTableMaterializer.php: Engine with the rest of the *Materializer family, for the same reason as TypedTableCapture.
layer_notes.src/Assess/AssessInventory.php: Surface with Cli.php: the read-only assess projection (round-3 MUP §4.5) is a command-shaped composition over policy, adapter and review, reached only from the wp duo verb that publishes it.
layer_notes.src/Capture/TypedTableCapture.php: Engine with the rest of the *Capture family even though it only reads kernel files; the recorded Snapshot -> TypedTableCapture edge names the real seam (a repository state model driving engine capture) instead of hiding it behind a convenient placement.
layer_notes.src/Code/CodeMaterializer.php: Repository, not engine, despite the *Materializer suffix: it depends only on PathSafety and is used solely by Code. The engine *Materializer family materializes authored state; this one materializes code bytes for the repository half.
layer_notes.src/Code/CodeOwnershipPruner.php: Repository for the same reason as CodeMaterializer: a Code-owned pruner over PathSafety, not an engine apply step.
layer_notes.src/Code/CodeStageTransaction.php: Repository: a Code-owned Db/Ledger transaction, kept with Code so the code half stays internally consistent.
layer_notes.src/Command/Cli.php: A surface file, and the top of the ladder: it may reference anything.
layer_notes.src/Grammar/Blocks.php: Policy, not kernel: block markup rewriting is driven by Policy and Tokens. Kept in one layer with Tokens/Shortcodes so the codec cycle resolves inside a layer instead of across two.
Policy with Tokens/Shortcodes: it registers policy-declared shortcode alternates.
layer_notes.src/Grammar/Shortcodes.php: Policy with Tokens/Blocks, for the same reason as Blocks.
layer_notes.src/Grammar/Tokens.php: Policy, not kernel, although the four codecs it composes (TextTokenizer, IdentityTokenCodec, StructuredReferenceCodec, UrlQueryReferenceCodec) are kernel: Tokens itself reads Policy to decide what a reference means. Its read of Ledger is the recorded inversion.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/Canon.php: Kernel by doctrine (canonical JSON/ordering is a primitive). Its single read of Policy is the oldest recorded inversion in the graph and the highest-value one to retire.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/DurableFilesystem.php: Kernel by doctrine. Its two upward edges to Publish/PublicationJournal are an artefact of the guarded InitialStateBoundaryException class being declared in three files; the scanner attributes a reference to every declaring file. Recorded rather than hidden, because collapsing that triple declaration is the real fix.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/OptionState.php: Kernel: it depends on Canon alone and is read by 26 files across every layer, including policy grammars. Placing it any higher would invert the *Grammar reads without describing anything true.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/ReferenceKeyspaceGrammar.php: Kernel with the rest of the reference grammar: it depends only on ReferenceRules, and the policy loader that reads it sits above.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/ReferenceScopeClassifier.php: Kernel: a dependency-free classifier read by Tokens, Shortcodes, Blocks and Capture.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/ReferenceShapeGrammar.php: Kernel with the rest of the reference grammar (ReferenceRules only).
layer_notes.src/Kernel/TableGraph.php: Kernel: a dependency-free table dependency graph.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/UserMetaState.php: Kernel: a dependency-free state model, read from the repository and engine layers.
layer_notes.src/Policy/ArtifactPolicyIdentity.php: Policy, not adapter: it is the identity a policy load stamps onto a compiled artifact. Its read of AdapterSources is the recorded inversion, not a reason to promote the file.
layer_notes.src/Policy/CodeConfigGrammar.php: Policy (the *Grammar axis) although it validates a Code envelope: its caller is SitePolicyValidator/Policy. The resulting read of Code is recorded rather than resolved by moving the grammar into the repository layer.
layer_notes.src/Policy/DeletionCapabilityResolver.ph: Policy (the *Resolver axis), not the Deletion* engine family: it answers a policy question from OptionNameReferenceResolver and is read by Policy itself.
layer_notes.src/Repository/CanonicalSurfaces.php: Repository: a catalogue over OptionState and SidebarState, so it sits with the state models it enumerates rather than with the planners that consume it.
layer_notes.src/Repository/Identity.php: Repository: identity is repository-side truth (Uuid + SidebarState + Canon), not an engine operation.
layer_notes.src/Repository/IdentityBackup.php: Repository with the rest of the Identity* family. It reads only policy/repository/kernel files, so the placement costs nothing.
layer_notes.src/Repository/ReferenceGraph.php: Repository, unlike the Reference* grammar/rules/path files: it is a graph over Snapshot and SidebarState, i.e. compiled repository state.
Repository with the Repository* family. Its read of the engine Deletion model is a real inversion and is recorded: the parser should take a deletion shape, not the engine type.
layer_notes.src/Repository/SidebarState.php: Repository: a state model over Ledger/Snapshot/Db, the same axis as Snapshot and OptionState consumers.
layer_notes.src/Repository/StateTreeWalker.php: Repository: a dependency-free walker over compiled state trees, read by Lint.

Kernel.purpose: Dependency-free primitives — canonical JSON, database access, reference codecs, durable filesystem, identifiers, secrets and PII redaction — that everything else is built on.

Policy.purpose: Loads, validates and pins the manifest and site policy that decides which WordPress state Duo owns, and answers every ownership question the engine asks.

Grammar.purpose: Declarative grammars and resolvers that turn manifest declarations and WordPress content syntax (blocks, shortcodes, tokens, options, taxonomies, user meta) into typed policy structures.

Repository.purpose: The durable repository of owned state: compiled artifacts, identity registry, ledger, reference graph, snapshots and their validators.

Code.purpose: Ownership, staging, compatibility and materialization of code artifacts (themes, plugins, mu-plugins) as repository state.

Capture.purpose: Reads owned state out of a live site into repository shape behind safety gates, a capture identity and a capture transaction.

Apply.purpose: Plans and executes writes of repository state into a live site: apply planning, services, the authored transaction and the per-entity materializers.

Scope.purpose: Scoped (partial-site) execution — the state overlay, session and work projection that let apply and capture run over a subset of the repository.

Rebuild.purpose: Derived-state regeneration: negotiating, selecting and dispatching native or provider rebuild actions after a write.

Publication.purpose: Atomic publication of a state tree to disk plus the journal that makes an interrupted publication recoverable.

Promotion.purpose: Deploy, lifecycle and promotion mechanics — planners, leases, locks, session journals and state handoff between environments.

Delete.purpose: Deletion authority, deletion guards and the executor that removes owned entities and records tombstones.

Init.purpose: First-contact onboarding of a site: probing, planning, confirming, journalling and recovering the initial owned baseline.

Review.purpose: Read-only projections over plans and state — lint and its reference scanners, coverage, pending, journal, orphans, canary, convergence verification and refresh export.

Adapter.purpose: The plugin-facing boundary: manifest sources, adapter registry, observation, site adapter certification and the provider SDK the engine calls through.

Command.purpose: The `wp duo …` WP-CLI surface: verb dispatch, argument parsing, refusal envelopes and operator output.

exceptions.reason: designed: Command dispatches the Assess projections; the reverse edge is forbidden.

Assess.purpose: Read-only inventory and projection commands answering 'what is here, and what can Duo do with it' before any write.

Transport.purpose: Carries bytes and commands to a target environment: the transport implementations, the environment driver handle and code deployment.

Plan.purpose: The plan wire contract and its operator/JSON renderings, with no I/O of its own.

Refresh.purpose: The B/P/W refresh planner, field diff and local state materializer that reconciles git, production and working state.

Environment.purpose: The environment registry and lifecycle that materialize, bind and reap the environments the orchestrator drives.

Recovery.purpose: Rollback authority and the verified/scoped rollback profiles that prove a target can be returned to a known state, plus (round 3) profile selection, the checkpoint catalog and the recovery claim the authorization plan embeds. Round-3 T5 adds the retained release checkpoints (RetainedCheckpoints), the second catalog source every transport has.

Onboarding.purpose: Adopting, initializing, diagnosing and triaging a site — the first-run and health mechanics behind adopt/init/doctor/classify/pending.

Adapter.purpose: Authoring-side adapter tooling: catalog, draft, observation, manifest validation against the agent's policy, and the operator's own Ed25519 certification authority (keygen/certify/pin).

Code.purpose: Host-side code-half sourcing: the wp.org release cache, fetch, verify, unpack and tree-digest primitives behind `duo init --code=split`, `duo code-classify` and (DUO-3500) `duo code-resolve`.

Command.purpose: The `duo` verb handlers, agent passthrough, option parsing, preflight and operator output. Composition across engine modules happens here: a `*Command` calls each engine module downward and hands the results to the next, which is why the populated cli modules need no intra-layer exceptions.

Assess.purpose: The assess mechanism — stack inventory and the authority block, the per-surface catalog carrying the six spec dimensions, the closed gap-action set, the `duo-assess-report/v1` document and its bounded human renderer. Mechanism only: `AssessCommand` (cli:Command) calls Doctor, the environment registry and the adapter catalog and hands their results in as data, which is what keeps this module free of intra-layer and upward edges (module map rule 9).

Release.purpose: The release mechanism — `AuthorizationPlan` (build, freeze before any mutation, digest and re-verify the `duo-authorization-plan/v1` document), `AuthorizationPlanRenderer` (its bounded human projection, ending in one question), `ReleaseOutcome` + `NextAction` (the closed post-freeze next-action set and the deterministic failure-class mapping) and `JourneyOracle` (the declared affected-journey probes and the `duo-verify-report/v1` document). Mechanism only: the verb boundaries (`ReleaseCommand`, `VerifyCommand`, `RecoverCommand`, cli:Command) compose it with Environment, Recovery and the existing promote/deploy handlers, and the recovery claim reaches the plan as a canonical array, not as a Recovery class reference — which is what keeps this module free of intra-layer and upward edges (module map rule 9).

Rehearse.purpose: The rehearsal mechanism — `RehearsalPlanPreview`, which joins the converged environment's plan-category projection with the assess-style surface rows restricted to that plan's actual scope to state what a release would touch, and `RehearsalDisclosure`, which owns MUP §2.2's containment banner and its consequence. Mechanism only, and pure: no I/O, no clock, no provider. The verb boundary (`RehearseCommand`, cli:Command) drives `EnvironmentLifecycle` and hands both documents in as data, which is what keeps this module free of intra-layer and upward edges (module map rule 9).

Contract.purpose: The per-site application contract as one object — manifests, site policy, evidence pins, bindings and capability report composed and addressable — plus `ProjectionVocabulary`, the single implementation of the spec-word projection that Assess, Release and Rehearse all read. Pure and offline-testable: a document, not a session.

not_moved.cli/duo: stays at cli/duo (the executable); its require list is rewritten by the codemod
